stem: A flat mirror lies along the line \(L\) with equation \(x + 2y = 10\). The points \(P(7, 9)\) and \(Q(10, 6)\) lie on the same side of \(L\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the gradient of \(L\), and the equation of the line through \(P\) that is perpendicular to \(L\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of \(F\), the point where this perpendicular line meets \(L\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence find the shortest distance from \(P\) to \(L\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: The point \(P'\) is the reflection of \(P\) in \(L\), so \(F\) is the midpoint of \([PP']\). Find the coordinates of \(P'\).

parts.label: e
parts.text: A ray of light leaves \(P\), reflects off the mirror at a point \(R\) on \(L\), and passes through \(Q\). The path \(P \to R \to Q\) is the shortest path from \(P\) to \(Q\) that touches \(L\), so \(R\) lies on the line \(P'Q\). Find the coordinates of \(R\).

parts.label: f
parts.text: Find the length of the path \(P \to R \to Q\).

idea: Perpendicular gradients multiply to \(-1\). The foot of the perpendicular is the closest point of the line, and reflecting \(P\) in \(L\) turns the bent path \(P \to R \to Q\) into the straight line \(P' \to R \to Q\) of the same length, because \(PR = P'R\).

solution.label: a
steps: \(2y = 10 - x\), so \(y = 5 - \frac{1}{2}x\) and the gradient of \(L\) is \(-\frac{1}{2}\).
A perpendicular line has gradient 2, since \(-\frac{1}{2} \times 2 = -1\). Through \(P(7, 9)\): \(y - 9 = 2(x - 7)\).

solution.label: c
steps: \(F\) is the point of \(L\) closest to \(P\), so the distance is \(PF = \sqrt{(7 - 4)^2 + (9 - 3)^2} = \sqrt{45}\).

solution.label: d
steps: \(F\) is the midpoint of \([PP']\), so \(P' = 2F - P = (2 \times 4 - 7,\ 2 \times 3 - 9)\).

solution.label: e
steps: Gradient of \(P'Q\): \(\dfrac{6 - (-3)}{10 - 1} = 1\), so the line is \(y + 3 = x - 1\), that is \(y = x - 4\).

solution.label: f
steps: \(PR = P'R\), because \(L\) is the perpendicular bisector of \([PP']\). So the path has the same length as \(P'Q\).

stem: The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are defined by \(f(x) = 2x - 1\), for \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), and \(g(x) = x^2 + 4\), for \(x \ge 0\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find \((g \circ f)(x)\), and state the values of \(x\) for which \(g \circ f\) is defined.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find \(f^{-1}(x)\) and \(g^{-1}(x)\), stating the domain of \(g^{-1}\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Solve the equation \((f \circ g)(x) = (g \circ f)(x)\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Solve the equation \(f(x) = f^{-1}(x)\).

parts.label: e
parts.text: Let \(h = f \circ g\). Find \(h^{-1}(x)\), state its domain, and show that \(h^{-1}(x) = \left(g^{-1} \circ f^{-1}\right)(x)\).

idea: In \(g \circ f\), \(f\) acts first, so its outputs must lie in the domain of \(g\). An inverse undoes a function, so the inverse of “\(g\) then \(f\)” is “undo \(f\), then undo \(g\)”.

solution.label: a
steps: \(g\) accepts only inputs \(\ge 0\), so we need \(2x - 1 \ge 0\), that is \(x \ge \frac{1}{2}\).

solution.label: b
steps: \(y = x^2 + 4\) with \(x \ge 0\) gives \(x = \sqrt{y - 4}\) (the positive root). The range of \(g\) is \(y \ge 4\), so this is the domain of \(g^{-1}\).

solution.label: c
steps: Both sides must be defined, so \(x \ge \frac{1}{2}\). \(1 - \sqrt{2} < 0\) is rejected.

solution.label: d
steps: This is where the line \(y = 2x - 1\) meets its reflection in \(y = x\): at \((1, 1)\), on the line \(y = x\).

stem: A fountain has a nozzle 1.5 m above the surface of a pool. The jet of water follows the curve \(h(x) = -0.5x^2 + 2x + 1.5\), where \(h\) metres is the height above the water surface and \(x\) metres is the horizontal distance from the nozzle.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write \(h(x)\) in the form \(a(x - p)^2 + q\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write down the greatest height of the jet and its horizontal distance from the nozzle at that point.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the horizontal distance from the nozzle to the point where the jet reaches the water surface.

parts.label: d
parts.text: A second nozzle is placed 6 m from the first, at the same height. Its jet is the reflection of the first jet in the line \(x = 3\). Write down an expression for the height of the second jet in terms of \(x\), and find the coordinates of the point where the two jets cross.

parts.label: e
parts.text: A swimmer’s raised hand reaches 1.2 m above the water. Find the set of values of \(x\) for which the hand is below both jets.

idea: Completing the square shows the vertex. Reflecting in the line \(x = 3\) sends \(x\) to \(6 - x\), so the second jet is \(h(6 - x)\). “Below both jets” means both heights are more than 1.2: solve each inequality and take the overlap.

solution.label: b
steps: The vertex is \((2, 3.5)\), and the parabola opens downwards, so this is the highest point.
solution.answer: 3.5 m, at 2 m from the nozzle

solution.label: d
steps: Reflection in \(x = 3\) sends \(x\) to \(6 - x\), so the second jet has height \(h(6 - x) = -0.5(4 - x)^2 + 3.5\).
By symmetry the jets cross on the mirror line \(x = 3\). Check: \(h(3) = -0.5 + 3.5 = 3\) and \(-0.5(4 - 3)^2 + 3.5 = 3\).
solution.answer: Second jet: \(-0.5(4 - x)^2 + 3.5\); the jets cross at \((3, 3)\)

solution.label: e
steps: Second jet above 1.2: \((4 - x)^2 < 4.6\), that is \(4 - \sqrt{4.6} < x < 4 + \sqrt{4.6}\).
Both: \(4 - \sqrt{4.6} < x < 2 + \sqrt{4.6}\). With \(\sqrt{4.6} = 2.144\ldots\), this is \(1.855\ldots < x < 4.144\ldots\)
These values lie between the nozzles (\(0 \le x \le 6\)), where both jets are in the air.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that \(f(x) = 2 + \dfrac{7}{x - 3}\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence describe a sequence of transformations that maps the graph of \(y = \dfrac{1}{x}\) onto the graph of \(y = f(x)\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Write down the equations of the asymptotes of the graph of \(f\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find \(f^{-1}(x)\) in the form \(c + \dfrac{d}{x - e}\), and state its domain.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Find the exact \(x\)-coordinates of the points where the graphs of \(y = f(x)\) and \(y = f^{-1}(x)\) meet.

parts.label: f
parts.text: Solve the inequality \(f(x) > 9\).

idea: Dividing out the fraction shows the graph is \(\frac{1}{x}\) stretched and moved. Its inverse has the asymptotes swapped. For the inequality, the sign of \(x - 3\) matters, so treat \(x > 3\) and \(x < 3\) separately.

solution.label: b
steps: Then \(y = \dfrac{7}{x - 3} + 2\): translation 3 units right and 2 units up, by the vector \(\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}\).
solution.answer: Vertical stretch by factor 7, then translation by \(\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}\)

solution.label: c
steps: The asymptotes of \(y = \frac{1}{x}\) are \(x = 0\) and \(y = 0\). The stretch does not move them, and the translation moves them 3 right and 2 up.

solution.label: d
steps: The range of \(f\) is every real number except 2, which becomes the domain of \(f^{-1}\).

solution.label: e
steps: \(x^2 - 5x - 1 = 0\), so \(x = \dfrac{5 \pm \sqrt{29}}{2}\). Neither is 2 or 3, so both are valid.
These are also the solutions of \(f(x) = x\): both points lie on the line \(y = x\).

solution.label: f
steps: If \(x < 3\), the left side is negative, so there are no solutions.
If \(x > 3\), multiply by the positive \(x - 3\): \(7 > 7(x - 3)\), so \(x - 3 < 1\) and \(x < 4\).

stem: A patient takes a 200 mg dose of a medicine at time \(t = 0\) hours. The amount of medicine in the body after \(t\) hours is \(A(t) = 200e^{-kt}\) mg. The amount halves every 6 hours.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that \(k = \dfrac{\ln 2}{6}\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the amount of medicine in the body after 10 hours.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The amount must not fall below 80 mg. Find the time at which the amount first falls to 80 mg.

parts.label: d
parts.text: At the time found in part (c), the patient takes a second 200 mg dose. The amount then decreases at the same rate. Find the time, measured from \(t = 0\), at which the amount next falls to 80 mg.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Instead, a doctor proposes a dose of 200 mg every \(T\) hours. Show that the amount just after the \(n\)th dose is \(200\left(1 + r + r^2 + \cdots + r^{n-1}\right)\) mg, where \(r = e^{-kT}\), and find the value of \(T\) for which this amount approaches 400 mg as \(n\) increases.

idea: Each half-life multiplies the amount by \(\frac{1}{2}\). After each dose the amount decays from its new starting value. With regular doses, every earlier dose has been multiplied by \(r\) once more, so the amounts form a geometric series.

solution.label: d
steps: Just after the second dose the amount is \(80 + 200 = 280\) mg. Let \(t_1 = 7.931\ldots\).

solution.label: e
steps: Between doses every amount is multiplied by \(e^{-kT} = r\). Just after dose \(n\), the newest dose gives 200, the one before it \(200r\), the one before that \(200r^2\), and the first dose \(200r^{n-1}\).
So the amount is \(200\left(1 + r + \cdots + r^{n-1}\right)\), a geometric series with \(0 < r < 1\).
As \(n\) increases this approaches \(\dfrac{200}{1 - r}\). Setting \(\dfrac{200}{1 - r} = 400\) gives \(r = \frac{1}{2}\).
\(e^{-kT} = \frac{1}{2}\) gives \(kT = \ln 2\), so \(T = \dfrac{\ln 2}{k} = 6\): one dose every half-life.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that \(g(x) = \log_2(4x - 4)\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Solve the equation \(f(x) = g(x)\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence solve the inequality \(f(x) > g(x)\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find \(g^{-1}(x)\), and state the range of \(g^{-1}\).

parts.label: e
parts.text: Find the set of values of \(k\) for which the equation \(f(x) - g(x) = k\) has a solution.

idea: Write a number as a logarithm (\(2 = \log_2 4\)) so that both sides become a single \(\log_2\). Since \(\log_2\) is increasing, \(\log_2 a > \log_2 b\) exactly when \(a > b\), for positive \(a\) and \(b\). For the last part, find every value that the single fraction inside the logarithm can take.

solution.label: b
steps: Check the domains: \(\frac{7}{3} > 1\), so both sides are defined.

solution.label: c
steps: Both functions are defined together only for \(x > 1\).
\(\log_2\) is increasing, so \(f(x) > g(x)\) exactly when \(x + 3 > 4x - 4\), that is \(x < \frac{7}{3}\).

solution.label: d
steps: The range of \(g^{-1}\) is the domain of \(g\).

solution.label: e
steps: As \(x\) runs over \(x > 1\), \(\dfrac{1}{x - 1}\) takes every positive value, so the fraction takes every value greater than \(\frac{1}{4}\), and never \(\frac{1}{4}\) itself.
So \(f(x) - g(x)\) takes every value greater than \(\log_2 \frac{1}{4} = -2\).

stem: Let \(f(x) = 4 - x^2\), for \(x \in \mathbb{R}\). The graph of \(g\) is obtained from the graph of \(f\) by a translation of 2 units to the right, then a reflection in the \(x\)-axis, then a translation of 1 unit up.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that \(g(x) = x^2 - 4x + 1\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: The point \((1, 3)\) lies on the graph of \(f\). Find the coordinates of its image on the graph of \(g\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Write down the coordinates of the vertex of the graph of \(g\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the exact \(x\)-coordinates of the points where the graphs of \(f\) and \(g\) meet.

parts.label: e
parts.text: The graph of \(g\) is translated \(a\) units to the right (where \(a\) may be negative) so that it touches the graph of \(f\) at exactly one point. Find the possible values of \(a\).

idea: Apply the transformations to the formula in the order given: \(f(x - 2)\), then \(-f(x - 2)\), then \(-f(x - 2) + 1\). Two curves touch at exactly one point when the equation for their meeting points has a repeated root, so its discriminant is zero.

solution.label: e
steps: Translating \(g\) by \(a\) units horizontally gives \(g(x - a) = (x - a - 2)^2 - 3\). Let \(b = a + 2\), so this is \((x - b)^2 - 3\).
Exactly one meeting point: discriminant zero. \(4b^2 - 8\left(b^2 - 7\right) = 0\), so \(56 - 4b^2 = 0\) and \(b^2 = 14\).
